title: 2026-11-25_XOR.DDoS_Botnet_Investigation_bdf
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a compromised Linux-based network. The network has been infected with the XOR.DDoS malware, which is known to turn infected hosts into bots participating in large DDoS attack campaigns. Your goal is to identify and analyze the malicious activities on the infected hosts.
outcomes: Identify suspicious services and their behaviors.
Discover communication endpoints used by the malware.
Investigate persistence mechanisms employed by the malware.

levels.title: Suspicious C2 Beacon Service Discovery
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for sending beacon periodically to the C2 Server.
levels.solution:
1. List all services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```
This command will list all services, including inactive ones.

2. Filter for running services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running
```
This will help you identify services that are currently active.

3. Check service descriptions and paths:
Look for services with unusual names or descriptions. Pay attention to the `ExecStart` path in the service definition.

4. Identify the suspicious service:
The service responsible for sending beacon to the C2 server is likely to have a name that does not match common system services.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services, including inactive ones.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions that do not match common system services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Check the `ExecStart` path in the service definition to identify the suspicious service.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Inspect the suspicious service:
```bash
systemctl cat bot-beacon.service
```
This command will show the service definition, including the `ExecStart` path.

2. Examine the beacon script:
```bash
cat /usr/local/lib/.botcache/beacon.sh
```
This script contains the communication details, including the port number.

3. Identify the C2 port:
Look for the port number in the `nc` command within the beacon script.

hints.content: Use `systemctl cat bot-beacon.service` to inspect the service definition.

hints.content: Examine the beacon script located at `/usr/local/lib/.botcache/beacon.sh`.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery for C2 Beaconing Service
levels.content: Investigators suspect how the C2 beacon service automatically resumes after the system starts and continues to execute periodically. Determine which system component is responsible for scheduling this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --all
```
This command will list all timers, including inactive ones.

2. Filter for active timers:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --state=active
```
This will help you identify timers that are currently active.

3. Inspect the timer associated with the beacon service:
```bash
systemctl cat bot-beacon.timer
```
This command will show the timer definition, including the `OnCalendar` schedule.

4. Identify the persistence mechanism:
The timer responsible for scheduling the beacon service is likely to have a name that matches the service name with `.timer` appended.

hints.content: Look for timers with names that match the service name with `.timer` appended.
